answer: Hardware-sealed timing quorum.** Each identity registers a physical clock module whose private key signs a continuous heartbeat; the module's drift curve is measured against a random network lantern schedule, so one operator cannot run many identities from shared timing. A quill signature ties every signed message to that drift trace, and any relic of a reused clock fingerprint collapses the whole batch. Attacker cost: one clock module, housing, and calibration per identity.
